# The tier-1 Python subset, exactly

You are writing a Python program that must run on a small Python interpreter.
Anything outside the list below makes the program fall back to a slower
interpreter, so stay inside it. Correctness comes first: never guess at an
approximation to stay inside the subset — a wrong answer is worse than a
fallback.

## Modules you may import

Only these: `sys`, `os`, `os.path`, `io`, `json`, `posixpath`, `random`.

Nothing else. In particular there is **no** `re`, `collections`, `math`,
`csv`, `pathlib`, `hashlib`, `datetime`, `struct`, `base64`, `itertools`,
`functools`, `textwrap`, `glob`, `statistics`, `subprocess`, `urllib`,
`shutil`, `tempfile`, `time` or `argparse`.

`random` is the seeded-integer subset only: `seed(<int>)` first, then
`random()`, `randint(a, b)`, `randrange(n)` / `randrange(a, b)`, `choice(<list,
tuple or str>)` and `getrandbits(k)` for `k <= 63`. No `shuffle`, `sample`,
`choices`, `uniform`, `gauss`, `Random(...)`, no `randrange` step, no keyword
arguments, and no stream without an integer seed — each of those falls back.

## Builtins you may call

Only these 39: `abs`, `all`, `any`, `bin`, `bool`, `bytes`, `chr`, `dict`, `divmod`, `enumerate`, `filter`, `float`, `format`, `hex`, `input`, `int`, `isinstance`, `iter`, `len`, `list`, `map`, `max`, `min`, `next`, `oct`, `open`, `ord`, `print`, `range`, `repr`, `reversed`, `round`, `set`, `sorted`, `str`, `sum`, `tuple`, `type`, `zip`.

Names that are NOT there and are commonly reached for: `eval`, `exec`,
`getattr`, `setattr`, `hasattr`, `vars`, `dir`, `globals`, `locals`,
`frozenset`, `bytearray`, `complex`, `hash`, `id`, `callable`, `slice`,
`super`, `staticmethod`, `property`, `pow` (use `**`), `bytearray`, `memoryview`
and `object`.

## Methods you may call

* `str`: `capitalize`, `casefold`, `count`, `encode`, `endswith`, `find`, `format`, `index`, `isalnum`, `isalpha`, `isdigit`, `islower`, `isnumeric`, `isspace`, `isupper`, `join`, `ljust`, `lower`, `lstrip`, `partition`, `removeprefix`, `removesuffix`, `replace`, `rfind`, `rindex`, `rjust`, `rpartition`, `rsplit`, `rstrip`, `split`, `splitlines`, `startswith`, `strip`, `swapcase`, `title`, `upper`, `zfill`
* `list`: `append`, `clear`, `copy`, `count`, `extend`, `index`, `insert`, `pop`, `remove`, `reverse`, `sort`
* `dict`: `clear`, `copy`, `get`, `items`, `keys`, `pop`, `popitem`, `setdefault`, `update`, `values`
* `set`: `add`, `clear`, `copy`, `difference`, `discard`, `intersection`, `issubset`, `issuperset`, `remove`, `symmetric_difference`, `union`, `update`
* `bytes`: `decode`, `endswith`, `find`, `hex`, `join`, `lower`, `lstrip`, `replace`, `rsplit`, `rstrip`, `split`, `startswith`, `strip`, `upper`
* `tuple`: `count`, `index`
* file objects: `close`, `read`, `readline`, `readlines`, `seek`, `tell`, `write`, `writelines`

Absent and refused — `str`: `center`, `expandtabs`, `format_map`, `isascii`, `isdecimal`, `isidentifier`, `isprintable`, `istitle`, `maketrans`, `translate`; `dict`: `fromkeys`; `set`: `difference_update`, `intersection_update`, `isdisjoint`, `pop`, `symmetric_difference_update`; `bytes`: `capitalize`, `center`, `count`, `expandtabs`, `fromhex`, `index`, `isalnum`, `isalpha`, `isascii`, `isdigit`, `islower`, `isspace`, `istitle`, `isupper`, `ljust`, `maketrans`, `partition`, `removeprefix`, `removesuffix`, `rfind`, `rindex`, `rjust`, `rpartition`, `splitlines`, `swapcase`, `title`, `translate`, `zfill`.

## Syntax that is inside

Assignment, `if`/`elif`/`else`, `for`, `while`, `break`, `continue`, `def`
(including default arguments, `*args` and `**kwargs`), `lambda`, `return`,
`global`, `try`/`except`/`finally`, `raise`, `assert`, `with open(...) as f`,
`del`, augmented assignment, slice assignment, tuple and starred unpacking,
chained comparisons, conditional expressions, list/dict/set comprehensions,
generator expressions, f-strings including format specs, `%` formatting,
`str.format`, bytes literals, triple-quoted strings, nested functions and
closures.

## Syntax that is outside

`class` definitions, decorators, `yield` and generator functions, `async`/
`await`, the walrus operator `:=`, keyword-only parameters (`def f(*, a)`),
`nonlocal`, self-documenting f-strings (`f"{x=}"`), `except*`, `...`
(Ellipsis), complex-number literals.

## Three refusals that no rewrite of an import can dodge

These are decided at run time, not by the imports, and they are deliberate:

1. **Integers are 64-bit.** Any arithmetic whose exact result leaves the signed
   64-bit range is refused. Factorials past 20, `2**64`, and big products are
   all outside.
2. **Set iteration order is refused.** Building a set is fine and `len(set(...))`
   is fine, but anything that would *expose* an order — printing a set,
   iterating one, `list(set(...))` — is refused. Wrap it in `sorted(...)`.
3. **`repr()` of non-ASCII text** outside a whitelist of plainly printable
   blocks is refused, and so is `os.listdir()`, whose order the filesystem
   defines rather than Python.

## The tier below, for reference

If a program leaves the subset above but only needs one of these modules, it
lands on a second small interpreter rather than on CPython: `argparse`, `base64`, `binascii`, `builtins`, `cmath`, `collections`, `contextlib`, `csv`, `datetime`, `errno`, `glob`, `hashlib`, `io`, `json`, `math`, `os`, `os.path`, `pathlib`, `random`, `re`, `shutil`, `statistics`, `struct`, `sys`, `tempfile`, `textwrap`, `time`, `urllib`, `urllib.parse`, `zlib`. That is still
much cheaper than CPython, so preferring `re` over `subprocess` is a real win
even when the subset proper is out of reach.
